title: Policies
heading: Policies
start_phrase: The Group’s organisation model and structure envisage that all corporate structures are responsible for basing their conduct on ethics and risk culture principles, as well as promoting a corporate culture based on ethics, inclusion, accountability and legality, in compliance with the Code of Ethics.
summary:
- Emphasis on an ethics- and risk-based corporate culture that respects human rights, promotes inclusion, accountability, legality, and enforces zero tolerance for discrimination across all protected grounds.
- Codification of commitments through key Group policies:
  - Rules on Inclusion: sets commitments to diversity, inclusion, equity and parity across the employee lifecycle, organization, operations, and communications; applies to the Parent Company and all Group companies; approved by the CHCO Directorate; aligned with EU and international frameworks (EU Charter of Fundamental Rights, UN Declaration of Human Rights, SDGs/2030 Agenda, Principles for Responsible Banking) and relevant EU/Italian regulations (CRD V, EBA guidelines, EU 2023/970, Bank of Italy Circular 285, Law 162/2021).
  - Gender Equality Policy: promotes fairness, equality and an inclusive climate of listening and respect for all stakeholders; approved by the Board of Directors; aligned with UNI/PdR 125:2022.
  - Rules on Preventing and Combating Gender-Based Harassment: defines non-tolerated conduct and principles to ensure a workplace free from discrimination, violence, and harassment; applies Group-wide; approved by the CHCO Directorate; compliant with Law 4/2021 and ILO Convention 190/2019.
  - Group Guidelines on the Management of Whistleblowing Systems: governs reporting and handling of actual/potential non-compliance including breaches of equal opportunity and inclusion; applicable to Parent Company and Group entities; drafted in line with CRD IV, Legislative Decree 72/2015 (Art. 52-bis TUB), Bank of Italy Circular 285 (11th/34th updates), and EU Directive 2019/1937. 
  - All documents are accessible via the Sustainability section of the corporate website.
- Reporting and remediation mechanisms:
  - Whistleblowing system for EU law and regulatory breaches, including equality and inclusion violations.
  - Additional channel via a Protection Committee for inappropriate workplace behavior.
  - Defined governance for implementing documents, managing deviations/non-conformities, and issuing specific reports.
- Continuous training for all new hires on mandatory topics (privacy, AML, Legislative Decree 231/2001, Code of Ethics, safety, Corporate Governance Code, etc.).
- Gender Equality Management System:
  - Updated for monitoring compliance and managing recommendations with corrective actions.
  - Establishes a Strategic Plan on gender equality with objectives and actions based on indicator analysis; overseen and approved by a Top Management Steering Committee.
  - Commitment to KPIs that track implementation of the Gender Equality Policy and support cultural change in diversity and inclusion.
- Ongoing Group-wide initiatives (2024–2028) covering employment and inclusion of people with disabilities, prevention of workplace violence and harassment, and promotion of diversity, applicable to all personnel.
text:
Policies 
The Group’s organisation model and structure envisage that all corporate structures are responsible for basing their conduct  
on ethics and risk culture principles, as well as promoting a corporate culture based on ethics, inclusion, accountability  
and legality, in compliance with the Code of Ethics. This Code, among its fundamental principles, demands respect  
for human rights in all activities and in relations with its stakeholders. 
To this end, the importance of disseminating an inclusive corporate culture as a strategic driver of development and  
“zero tolerance” towards any kind of discrimination (racial and ethnic origin, colour, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, di-
sability, age, religion, political opinion, national extraction or social origin, or other forms of discrimination covered by Union re-
gulation and national law) are reaffirmed in the internal document “Rules on Inclusion” as well as in the Gender Equality Policy.

Actual or potential “non-compliance”, such as violations of the principles of equal opportunities, fairness and inclusion 
set out in the Code of Ethics and other cases that may constitute violations of European Union law and relevant external  
and internal regulations, are handled through the whistleblowing system, as provided for in the Group Directive on the  
Management of Internal Whistleblowing Systems. 
As for the reporting of inappropriate behaviour in the workplace, the reporting person, in addition to using the  
whistleblowing system, can report to a special Protection Committee, as specified in the document Rules on preventing 
and combating gender-based harassment in the workplace, and in the document Gender Equality Management System. 
The implementation and governance of the regulatory documents and related processes just mentioned describe  
the general approach for remedial measures with respect to any deviations/non-conformities that may occur. In keeping 
with this fundamental approach, all new recruits, from the beginning of their employment, receive information and conti -
nuous training on the duties they are required to perform, on the regulatory elements governed by the National Collective 
Bargaining Agreement and on specific disclosures (i.e., on privacy, anti-money laundering, Legislative Decree 231/2001, 
Code of Ethics, prevention and safety, Corporate Governance Code, etc.).

title: Actions
heading: Actions
start_phrase: To ensure the monitoring of gender equality activities and areas, with particular reference to compliance management, the Gender Equality Management System was updated.
summary:
- Scope and purpose: Group Guidelines on the management of whistleblowing systems for handling actual or potential non-compliance, including breaches of equal opportunities, fairness, and inclusion in the Code of Ethics, as well as violations of EU law and internal/external regulations.
- Applicability and governance: Applies to all personnel of the Parent Company and Group companies (Banca Widiba, Monte Paschi Fiduciaria). Implementation to be notified to the Directorate of Corporate Reporting; Staff CAE and Government Audit Subsidiaries; Organisation Partner; and Organisation Function. Documents available in the Group website Sustainability section.
- Regulatory framework: Aligned with Directive 2013/36/EU (CRD IV), Italian Legislative Decree 72/2015 (Article 52-bis TUB), Bank of Italy Circular 285 (11th and 34th updates), and Directive 2019/1937/EU (EU whistleblowing).
- Reporting channels: Whistleblowing system covers non-compliance; inappropriate workplace behavior may also be reported to a Protection Committee per the Rules on preventing and combating gender-based harassment and the Gender Equality Management System.
- Training and compliance culture: New recruits receive ongoing training on contractual, regulatory, and ethical obligations (privacy, AML, Legislative Decree 231/2001, Code of Ethics, safety, Corporate Governance Code).
- Gender Equality Management System: Updated to monitor gender equality activities, define recommendations and corrective actions, and manage a Strategic Plan (2024–2028) with objectives and actions approved by a Top Management Steering Committee. Nonconformities are managed with specific reporting.
- KPIs and objectives: Adoption of specific D&I KPIs to track progress; key KPI is the share of positions of responsibility held by women—target 35% by 2023 exceeded (37%); 37.6% at end-2024; target >40% by 2028. Continuous monitoring with corrective measures as needed.
- Group-wide initiatives (ongoing over 2024–2028): 
  - Plural Management Project (D&I awareness, gender and disability focus).
  - Growth Together (evolution of the Women Leadership Program; 609 women managers since 2020).
  - Top Management training on gender equality and anti-harassment (Fondazione Libellula).
  - “Safe at work” specialist training on harassment prevention (Fondazione Libellula).
  - Disability LAB network participation (Wise Growth) on disability management topics.
  - “I’m Possible” trainings to build inclusive team awareness (disability focus).
  - Unconscious Bias course (97% completion) and Gender Equity course (92% completion) for all staff.
  - Anti-harassment awareness: ABI “Words of Inclusion” podcasts; “Financial Education: an empowerment tool” to counter economic violence.
  - D&I intranet page with interactive content and an inclusive glossary.
  - D&I induction for new recruits.
  - Inclusion Week (March 2024) on harassment prevention and disability; publication of a disability manifesto.
  - Participation in “Open Jam 2024” (The European House – Ambrosetti) to foster intergenerational dialogue.
text:
Actions
To ensure the monitoring of gender equality activities and areas, with particular reference to compliance management, the 
Gender Equality Management System was updated. Based on the outcome of the monitoring carried out, the management 
of recommendations was defined, ensuring the activation of any corrective actions. With a view to continuous improve-
ment in the areas of gender equality and inclusion, the System envisages the preparation, management and updating of a 
Strategic Plan on gender equality , defining objectives and decisive action to close the gaps identified from analysis of the 
dedicated indicators. the Plan is shared and approved by a special Steering Committee, composed of Top Management.  
At the same time, nonconforming situations, such as violations of the principles of equal opportunities, equity and inclusion,  
are managed, and specific reporting is drafted. 
With the aim of monitoring the implementation of the principles expressed in the Gender Equality Policy over time,  
the Group is committed to adopting specific KPIs that, in line with and consistent with the principles contained in the  
reference regulatory documents, enable the monitoring and measurement of the progress and results achieved, in support 
of the cultural change in terms of diversity and inclusion. 
Below are the main actions related to the employment and inclusion of people with disabilities, prevention of violence  
and harassment in the workplace and promoting diversity.
These initiatives are implemented at Group level, affect all personnel and have a continuity character over the reference 
time horizon coinciding with the Strategic Plan in execution (2024-2028)2024 ANNUAL REPORT - Sustainability Reporting 195

title: Initiatives dedicated to equal treatment and opportunities for all
heading: Initiatives dedicated to equal treatment and opportunities for all
start_phrase: In-house training continued in 2024 to raise awareness of respect for diversity and inclusion, particularly in relation to gender and disability, and a focus on the Gender Equality Policy.
summary:
- Focus area: Diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) initiatives to ensure equal treatment and opportunities, with emphasis on gender equality and disability inclusion.
- Manager and leadership development:
  - Plural Management Project: in-house DEI awareness training; 2,633 managers completed (210 in 2024).
  - Growth Together: continuation of the Women Leadership Program; 609 women managers participated since 2020 to build self-awareness and leadership goals.
  - Top Management training: targeted sessions on gender equality and prevention of workplace gender harassment (Fondazione Libellula).
  - “Safe at work”: specialist training on preventing and managing harassment (Fondazione Libellula).
- Disability inclusion:
  - Ongoing Disability LAB meetings (Wise Growth) on management training, identifying disability situations, and team support.
  - “I’m Possible” training to deepen knowledge of inclusive team experiences, focusing on disability.
- Company-wide awareness courses:
  - Unconscious Bias: available to all; 97% completion.
  - Gender Equity: available to all; 92% completion.
- Anti-violence and financial empowerment:
  - Participation in ABI’s “Words of Inclusion” for the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women.
  - Training on “Financial Education: an empowerment tool” to prevent and combat economic violence.
- Internal communication and onboarding:
  - Dedicated D&I intranet page with updates, resources, and a monthly inclusive glossary entry.
  - D&I module included in induction for new hires.
- Engagement initiatives:
  - Inclusion Week (March 2024): virtual classrooms on harassment prevention (Fondazione Libellula) and disability (internal trainers); publication of a disability manifesto with proposals and suggestions.
  - Participation in “Open Jam 2024” (The European House – Ambrosetti) to enhance intergenerational dialogue (GenZ, Millennials, GenX, Boomers).
- Objectives and KPI monitoring:
  - Strengthened DEI performance indicators aligned with “Rules on Inclusion” and ongoing monitoring.
  - Key KPI: percentage of positions of responsibility held by women—target 35% by 2023 exceeded (37% at end-2023; 37.6% at end-2024); new target of >40% by 2028 (per 2024–2028 Business Plan).
  - Targets set via KPI analysis to drive continuous improvement; relevant functions monitor indicators and implement corrective actions as needed in line with the Gender Equality Strategic Plan.
  - Clarification of which roles count as “positions of responsibility” across General Management, Regional Sales & Distribution, Regional Credit Divisions, and network branch/specialized center leadership.
text:
Initiatives dedicated to equal treatment and opportunities for all
Plural Management Project In-house training continued in 2024 to raise awareness of respect for diversity and inclusion, particularly in relation to 
gender and disability, and a focus on the Gender Equality Policy. A total of 2,633 managers have completed the course, 
including 210 in 2024. 
 Growth Together “Growth Together” was implemented as a continuation of the “Women Leadership Program”, a laboratory to support the 
managerial development of women in positions of responsibility, fostering self-awareness, knowing their own skills and 
setting firm objectives. Since its launch in 2020, the project has seen the participation of 609 women managers from all 
the business lines.
Top Management training The active involvement of top management on diversity and inclusion issues was accompanied by a dedicated information 
and training activity, focusing on gender equality and the fight against and prevention of gender harassment in the 
workplace, by Fondazione Libellula.
“Safe at work” training In 2024, a training meeting was held for specialists on how to intervene to prevent and manage possible incidents of 
harassment, organised by Fondazione Libellula.
Disability Lab meetings In 2024, the meetings of the ‘Disability LAB’, a network of companies set up to foster discussion on concrete action plans, 
by Wise Growth, continued.
In particular, the following topics were covered: “Management training in the disability field”, “The detection of disability 
situations in the company”, “Teams with disabilities: when and how to support them?”.
“I'm Possible” training 
meetingsIn 2024, training courses for resource persons were carried out to increase awareness and knowledge of the different 
experiences with inclusive teams, with a focus on disability issues.
Unconscious Bias The Unconscious Bias course was made available to the entire corporate population with the aim of learning about the 
phenomenon of bias and reflecting on how it can influence perception and opinions in our relations.  The online course 
was taken by 97% of the corporate population.
Gender equity In 2024, the 'Gender Equity' course was made available to the entire corporate population, which was taken by 92% of the 
corporate population.
Awareness-raising on 
the prevention of gender 
harassment On 25 November, the ‘International Day for the elimination of Violence Against Women’, the Bank joined ABI’s initiative 
‘Words of Inclusion’ to promote financial autonomy, a series of podcasts dedicated to the theme of economic violence.
The training courses ‘Financial Education: an empowerment tool’ focused on the enhancement of financial education as a 
tool to prevent and combat the phenomenon of economic violence.
D&I page on the corporate 
intranetThe intranet section fully dedicated to Diversity & Inclusion is constantly updated, where opinions can be expressed and 
suggestions put forward, including reading recommendations, videos, newsletters and so on. Each month, the section is 
enriched with a new word from the inclusive glossary, which aims to clarify the meaning of certain terms that have entered 
into common usage but are not always used correctly.
D&I training for new recruits The induction courses for new recruits include a special educational, taught in-house, dedicated to the topics of Diversity 
& Inclusion.
Inclusion Week A week of virtual classrooms was held in March 2024, involving all Group personnel, on a voluntary basis, to reflect on 
two macro areas: workplace harassment contrast and prevention (by Fondazione Libellula) and disability (by internal 
teachers). At the end of the classrooms, a disability manifesto was published, in which suggestions and proposals were 
collected to promote initiatives that accommodate the needs of each colleague. 
Open Jam As part of the projects aimed at strengthening its commitment to valuing diversity and spreading an inclusive culture, 
the Group also joined the 'Open Jam 2024' initiative, promoted by The European House - Ambrosetti, with the intention of 
enhancing the comparison between the different generations present in the company (GenZ, Millennials, GenX, Boomers).

start_phrase: The focus on issues related to diversity and inclusion is reinforced with an enrichment of performance indicators in line with the “Rules on Inclusion” document and with constant monitoring of existing indicators.
summary:
- Diversity and Inclusion initiatives: The Group ran extensive training and awareness programs on gender equality, disability inclusion, harassment prevention, and unconscious bias. Key actions included:
  - Plural Management Project training (2,633 managers trained overall; 210 in 2024) on diversity, inclusion, and Gender Equality Policy.
  - “Growth Together” leadership development for women (609 participants since 2020).
  - Top management engagement and training on gender equality and anti-harassment by Fondazione Libellula; a “Safe at work” session for specialists on harassment prevention/management.
  - Ongoing Disability LAB meetings (Wise Growth) on disability management, detection, and team support; “I’m Possible” sessions to build inclusive team awareness.
  - Unconscious Bias training offered to all staff (97% completion) and a “Gender Equity” course (92% completion).
  - Awareness efforts on preventing gender harassment and economic violence, including joining ABI’s “Words of Inclusion” and financial education courses as empowerment tools.
  - A continually updated D&I intranet hub with resources and an inclusive glossary; D&I modules in new hire induction.
  - Inclusion Week virtual classrooms (harassment prevention and disability) culminating in a disability manifesto with proposals; participation in “Open Jam 2024” to foster intergenerational dialogue.

- Objectives and KPIs: Strengthened D&I performance measurement aligned with the “Rules on Inclusion,” with close monitoring and corrective actions as needed.
  - Core KPI: share of positions of responsibility held by women—targeted at 35% by 2023 (achieved 37% in 2023; 37.6% at end-2024); goal set at >40% by 2028 under the 2024–2028 Business Plan.
  - Targets defined via KPI analysis and coordinated by relevant functions; scope of “positions of responsibility” explicitly defined across management layers and network roles.

- Privacy governance and practices: A dedicated section outlines protection of employees’ personal data through the Group’s Data Protection Policy.
  - Policy scope, governance, and standards: Currently applies to the Bank with plans to extend Group-wide; Board of Directors oversees privacy compliance, approves policies, and provides strategic direction. Compliance aligns with GDPR, the Italian Privacy Code (as amended), and guidance from the Italian Data Protection Authority and EDPB. Policy is published on the corporate website (Sustainability section).
  - Methodological approach: Privacy by design/technology, data subject rights management, Records of processing, and data breach handling; defined roles/responsibilities, information flows, planning/reporting, and employee empowerment.
  - Actions and controls: Regular employee training at induction, job changes, or when new tools are introduced, covering regulatory and technological risks (e.g., phishing). Data access follows strict need-to-know principles with role-based authorizations tied to tasks and organizational units.

Objectives
The focus on issues related to diversity and inclusion is reinforced with an enrichment of performance indicators in line 
with the “Rules on Inclusion” document and with constant monitoring of existing indicators. In particular, mention is made 
of the indicator concerning the percentage of positions of responsibility43 held by women. This KPI - already identified as 
a Smart target  for the period 2021-2023, in line with the commitments undertaken after joining the UNEP FI Principles for 
Responsible Banking and with the provisions of the UNI/PdR 125/2022 Reference Practice on Gender Equality Certifica -
tion - was	set	at	35%	by	2023	and	was	comfortably	 passed,	with	the	actual	figure	at	the	end	of	this	period	reaching	 37%	
and increasing further to 37.6% at the end of 2024 . This indicator will continue to be one of the most monitored KPIs for 
achieving the objective set in the 2024-2028 Business Plan, i.e. more than 40% in 2028. 
Targets are defined on the basis of KPI analysis, also with a view to pursuing the goal of continuous improvement in the 
areas of gender equality and inclusion, through the involvement of the functions that directly oversee the relevant issues. 
Monitoring of the defined indicators is managed by the relevant functions, which, in the event of deviations, identify cor -
rective actions to align with the objectives of the Gender Equality Strategic Plan.

start_phrase: In order to prevent the violation of data privacy rights, data protection safeguards and channels for employees to raise concerns are ensured through the “Data Protection Policy”.
summary:
- Focus: Protection of personal data confidentiality for the Group’s people, with safeguards and channels for employees to raise privacy concerns.
- Core policy: Data Protection Policy outlining a methodological approach covering:
  - Privacy by design/technology and compliance with data protection principles.
  - Respect for data subject rights.
  - Maintenance of Records of Processing Activities.
  - Data breach management.
  - Defined roles and responsibilities, privacy information flows, planning, reporting, and employee training/empowerment.
- Scope: Currently applies to the Bank, with plans to extend to other Group companies.
- Governance: Board of Directors oversees the privacy compliance system, approves policies/processes, provides strategic guidance, and issues implementation instructions.
- Compliance framework: Adherence to EU GDPR, Italian Privacy Code (Legislative Decree 196/2003 as amended by 101/2018), and guidelines/decisions from the Italian Data Protection Authority, EDPB, and other relevant regulations.
- Availability: Policy published in the Sustainability section of the Group’s corporate website.
- Actions and controls: Ongoing employee training at onboarding, role changes, and new tool introductions; content spans regulatory obligations and technological risks (e.g., phishing, scams).
- Access management: Only authorized personnel process personal data on a need-to-know basis; each employee has a unique system user with role-based authorization tied to tasks and organizational unit; controls apply to both digital and paper data.

title: Actions
heading: Actions
start_phrase: In order to ensure that employees are trained in data protection issues, the Group provides for employee training, i.e. initiatives to promote a data protection culture.
summary:
- Focus: Privacy protection of employees’ personal data within Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena, as part of the 2024 Sustainability Report.
- Policy framework: A Group Data Protection Policy outlines:
  - Operational and privacy controls to ensure compliance from project/design and technology use stages, protection of data subject rights, maintenance of processing records, and data breach management.
  - Defined roles and responsibilities, privacy information flows, planning/reporting of activities and controls, and employee training/empowerment.
  - Current scope limited to the Bank with plans to extend to other Group companies.
  - Governance by the Board of Directors; compliance with GDPR, Italian Privacy Code (as amended), and guidance from the Italian Data Protection Authority and EDPB.
  - Public availability in the Group website’s Sustainability section.
- Actions and controls:
  - Ongoing employee training on regulatory aspects (privacy compliance, confidentiality, data breach handling) and technological risks (phishing and scams), provided at induction, during role changes, and upon introduction of new data-processing tools.
  - Strict access management based on necessity and role-specific authorization profiles for the Bank’s Information System; definition of “persons authorised to process data.”
- Objectives and monitoring:
  - No specific quantitative privacy targets set; effective oversight maintained.
  - Compliance Function conducts Level II checks: remote/on-site audits, reporting non-compliance to Internal Audit and DPO Staff, verifying DPIAs, and supporting DPO reporting to senior management.
- Worker involvement and industrial relations:
  - Respect for freedom of association and ILO-aligned practices; robust engagement with trade unions through Level II bargaining.
  - Structured consultations and disclosures during reorganizations, mobility, and changes in work organization; negotiation windows up to 50 days per the National Collective Labour Agreement.
  - Industrial relations managed by the First Level Company Function, ensuring compliance and active dialogue.
  - Joint Committees (Commercial Policies, Welfare, Training, Equal Opportunities, Environmental Sustainability) met 11 times in 2024 to address material issues and promote development.
  - The Equal Opportunities Committee sets female employment indicators and empowerment policies; the Corporate Observatory monitors workplace interactions, communication quality, and risks to worker dignity.
text:
Actions
In order to ensure that employees are trained in data protection issues, the Group provides for employee training,  
i.e. initiatives to promote a data protection culture. In particular, such training courses are part of the Group’s established 
practice and are provided for employees both at the time of their induction, as well as on the occasion of job changes  
or the introduction of significant new tools for the processing of personal data. 
Training courses on this subject cover not only purely regulatory aspects (e.g. compliance with privacy regulations, data 
confidentiality, handling a data breach) but also those relating to data protection from a technological point of view,  
e.g. with regard to phishing or other scam techniques. 
Persons authorised to process data are all employees who, in connection with their activities, come into contact with and 
process personal data to which they have access.  Access to personal data, whether in computerised form or on paper,  
by persons authorised to process the data, must only take place if knowledge of the data is strictly necessary to perform  
the tasks assigned. In this respect, each appointee is assigned an access user to the Bank’s Information System,  
the authorisation profile of which is closely related to the role he/she holds, the tasks entrusted to him/her and the  
operational entity to which he/she belongs.2024 ANNUAL REPORT - Sustainability Reporting 197

title: Objectives
heading: Objectives
start_phrase: The group has not, to date, defined specific objectives for dealing with employee privacy issues.
summary:
- Employee privacy governance: No specific objectives set yet, but ongoing Level II compliance monitoring by the Compliance Function, including remote/on-site audits, reporting non-compliance to Internal Audit and the DPO, verification of DPIA execution, and support to the DPO in management reporting.
- Worker engagement and representation: The Group supports freedom of association in line with the Italian Constitution and ILO principles, encouraging active dialogue with trade unions.
- Collective bargaining and consultation: Level II bargaining emphasizes ongoing social dialogue, information, and consultation rights to support long-term sustainable growth and a positive corporate climate.
- Change management: In cases of restructuring or reorganization, the Group provides required disclosures and conducts negotiations with trade unions (up to 50 days) before implementing measures, aiming to limit impacts and safeguard working conditions.
- Industrial relations oversight: Managed by the First Level Company Function, which plans and conducts consultation procedures and ensures compliance with laws and collective agreements.
- Joint Committees: Company–union bodies central to Level II bargaining; met 11 times in 2024; focus areas include Commercial Policies, Welfare, Training, Equal Opportunities, and Environmental Sustainability.
- Equal Opportunities Committee: Sets female employment indicators and develops empowerment policies, advancing diversity as a driver of cultural and social growth.
- Corporate Observatory: Joint body monitoring workplace interactions and communication, aiming to preserve individual dignity and quality of life, and to identify situations that could harm worker dignity.
text:
Objectives
The group has not, to date, defined specific objectives for dealing with employee privacy issues. Nevertheless, the Group 
oversees the effective monitoring of policies and actions in relation to this issue. In particular, responsibility for Level II 
checks on the regulatory requirements of privacy obligations is assigned to the Compliance Function. These controls are 
part of the Group’s normal operations and consist of:
• planning and carrying out remote and on-site audits during the year, also taking into account requests made by the  
Data Protection Officer (hereinafter also DPO);
• if aspects of non-compliance emerge in the conduct of employees in the performance of the duties entrusted to them 
in the field of privacy, reporting to the Internal Audit Function and the DPO Staff;
• carrying out Level II checks on the correct execution of the Data Protection Impact Assessment (hereinafter also DPIA);
• as part of the reporting to senior management prepared by the DPO, support to the DPO with regard to the results of 
privacy compliance checks carried out.

title: Processes for involving own workers and workers’ representatives on impacts - Introduction
heading: Processes for involving own workers and workers’ representatives on impacts
start_phrase: The management of material impacts entails that the Group should have its own employee engagement processes in place to take their views into account.
summary: Overview of Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena’s processes to involve employees and trade union representatives on material impacts, grounded in Italy’s constitutional protections of association (Articles 18 and 39) and ILO membership. The Group encourages freedom of association and uses Level II bargaining to promote dialogue, information, and consultation rights with Trade Unions, especially around reorganizations, restructurings, and mobility; it provides disclosures per the National Collective Labour Agreement and implements agreed measures only after predefined negotiation periods (up to 50 days). Industrial relations are managed by the First Level Company Function, ensuring compliance and active consultation. Joint Committees of company and unions met 11 times in 2024 across areas including Commercial Policies, Welfare, Training, Equal Opportunities, and Environmental Sustainability. The Equal Opportunities Committee sets female employment indicators and empowerment policies, while the Corporate Observatory monitors workplace interactions and communications to preserve individual dignity and quality of life and identify potentially harmful situations.
text:
Processes for involving own workers and workers’ representatives on impacts 
The management of material impacts entails that the Group should have its own employee engagement processes  
in place to take their views into account.
At constitutional level, Italy protects the freedom of association (Article 18) and trade union membership (Article 39) and 
is a member of the International Labour Organization (ILO). In line with constitutional principles and regulations in force, 
the Group encourages freedom of association for employees, which it manifests in many ways. 
Level II bargaining, which is entirely consistent with the applicable regulatory framework, confirms the strategic value of dia-
logue and the active involvement of trade union organisations, at the basis of a corporate climate of positive participation.  
To this end, the Group is committed to promoting information and consultation rights of the Trade Unions so that, each  
in their respective roles, the best solutions are constantly sought, in the common interest of laying the foundations for the 
long-term sustainable growth of the Group.
Ongoing discussion between the Parties, at central and peripheral level, has the shared objective of fostering extensive 
awareness and assessment of the repercussions on resources of reorganisations and seeking suitable convergences  
to limit the impacts and guarantee quality of working conditions in a context of innovation and change. In all cases of 
restructuring, business reorganisation or other activities affecting personnel in terms of work organisation and regional 
and professional mobility, the Group arranges specific disclosures, in compliance with provisions of the National Collective 
Labour Agreement, and/or discussions with trade unions to analyse the impact on staff. It is after the closure of negotia -
tions, with different durations contractually predefined on the basis of the reorganisation (up to 50 days), that the agreed 
measure can be implemented.
The Group’s industrial relations are supervised and managed by the First Level Company Function, through the planning 
and management of activities (initiation, development and definition of consultation procedures) and active listening to 
company trade union representatives to ensure compliance with laws and national and Level II bargaining.
In this context, Joint Committees, made up of company and union members, play a fundamental role in Level II bargaining, 
dealing with specific areas to jointly examine material issues and promote initiatives for enhancement and growth within 
company policies and processes.
The Committees - which met in 11 sessions in 2024 - are divided by scope and subject matter, including: “Commercial 
Policies”, “Welfare”, “Training”, “Equal Opportunities” and “Environmental Sustainability”.
Specifically, the ‘Equal Opportunities’ Committee has the task of agreeing female employment indicators at company level, 
as well as identifying appropriate empowerment policies. The Committee’s activity was strengthened for the purpose of 
finding tangible solutions to enhancing the potential of people, each with their own diversities, identified as factors for 
the Group’s cultural and social growth. Equally significant is the analysis conducted by the Corporate Observatory, a joint 
body set up to monitor interaction between personnel in the different operating entities with communications models that  
engage individuals at all levels. Its focus is on relationships to preserve the individual personality and maintain a high  
standard of “quality” of life in the company, and also on situations that may potentially harm the dignity of workers.

title: Listening to employees
heading: Listening to employees
start_phrase: For the Group, listening to people is an essential element of the relationship with employees and is carried out systematically by applying different internal tools and channels.
summary:
- Focus on systematic employee listening as a core element of the employer–employee relationship, using multiple internal tools and channels.
- CEO engagement throughout 2024: 14 in‑person meetings in Italy with 4,000+ colleagues to share 2024–2028 Business Plan and encourage dialogue; six additional in‑person sessions with Talent Academy participants and new hires; four all‑staff conference calls on financial results with live Q&A and follow‑up FAQs on the intranet.
- Division leadership outreach: 24 live meetings by Commercial C‑levels to explain divisional priorities and gather questions/remarks via live and post‑event channels.
- Sales function listening: 45 targeted sessions (often with business partners) to present market outlooks and collect feedback.
- “A Day at the Branch” (July 2024): managers from central structures visited 60+ branches, engaging ~2,500 employees for practical, network‑focused dialogue; attended by the CEO and Deputy Chief Commercial Officer; key insights compiled and shared via a structured intranet article.
- Measuring effectiveness and continuous feedback: internal climate surveys, focus groups, post‑event satisfaction questionnaires, and interactive intranet features (comments, likes, shares); new “Did you find this article useful?” prompt to assess content relevance and clarity.
- Open channels for all employees to express views on work life, applications, and initiatives; ongoing one‑to‑one meetings with HR Managers, including upon employee request.
- Targeted listening for new employees: early‑tenure satisfaction questionnaires and probation‑period feedback interviews to surface needs and areas of attention.
text:
Listening to employees
For the Group, listening to people is an essential element of the relationship with employees and is carried out systematically  
by applying different internal tools and channels. 
With a view to continuous updating and sharing the most important topics for the Group, the Chief Executive Officer  
continued to be involved. In particular, the CEO - over the course of 2024 - held 14 meetings in Italy (involving more  
than 4,000 colleagues) with the aim of sharing the guidelines of corporate strategy (2024-2028 Business Plan), fostering 
dialogue, listening and active participation.
These meetings were complemented by a further six in-person events at which the CEO met colleagues on development 
paths (“Talent Academy”) and new recruits. 
The CEO also held four conference call meetings with all colleagues to present the financial results for the period.  
On these occasions, a Q&A session was also scheduled , in which participants could put questions directly to the CEO. 
In-depth meetings on the topics posed by the HR Managers were then scheduled for these colleagues. Answers to  
frequently asked questions are made available on the Intranet.
The Commercial C-levels held 24 live meetings with colleagues from the respective Divisions to share and improve  
understanding of the j lines and the corporate objectives for the period. At each of these meetings, colleagues were able  
to submit questions or remarks, commented directly or after the event on the other communications channels. 
Some sales functions hold specific listening sessions - sometimes with the assistance of business partners - to present 
market outlooks.  45 meetings in total were held in 2024.
In July 2024, the first edition of “A Day at the Branch” was held: more than 60 branches (for a total of about 2,500 people 
involved) throughout Italy hosted an equal number of managers from the central structures in order to carry out a direct 
and fruitful discussion focusing on practical aspects of the network’s activities, so as to enhance together each concrete 
element and thus pursue the growth of the Bank and its people. The meetings were also attended by the Chief Executive 
Officer and the Deputy Chief Commercial Officer.
The main information and questions from the Network were taken up by the Departments and provided structured  
feedback to all staff through an article published on the intranet.

title: The effectiveness of involvement
heading: The effectiveness of involvement
start_phrase: Internal climate surveys and feedback collection are carried out by means of focus groups and employee satisfaction questionnaires after events, as well as interactive functions on the company intranet (comments, likes, shares).
summary:
- Employee listening and engagement: The Group systematically gathers employee input through multiple tools and channels. In 2024, the CEO held 14 in-person meetings across Italy with over 4,000 colleagues to share the 2024–2028 Business Plan, plus six sessions with Talent Academy participants and new hires, and four companywide calls on financial results with Q&A. Follow-ups included HR-led deep dives and intranet FAQs.
- Leadership dialogue across the organization: Commercial C-levels ran 24 live divisional meetings with open Q&A. Sales functions hosted 45 listening sessions, sometimes with business partners, to discuss market outlooks. The “A Day at the Branch” initiative in July 2024 brought central managers to over 60 branches (about 2,500 participants), including attendance by the CEO and Deputy Chief Commercial Officer; key takeaways were shared with all staff via the intranet.
- Measuring effectiveness of involvement: The Group uses climate surveys, focus groups, post-event satisfaction questionnaires, and interactive intranet features (comments, likes, shares, and a “Did you find this article useful?” prompt). HR Managers conduct systematic one-to-one meetings, including at employee request. New hires receive targeted listening through early-tenure questionnaires and probation-period feedback interviews.
- Channels to raise concerns and remediation processes: The Group encourages open dialogue through territorial meetings and formal structures. It operates a confidential Whistleblowing system (IT platform and telephone) for employees and qualified external personnel to report suspected misconduct, managed by the Fraud Audit department, with dedicated training—including a new multimedia course in 2024—plus additional training for control owners and new employees.
- Protection of workers’ human rights: The Group commits to skill enhancement, professional development, and ESG culture, aligning with the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights, UN Global Compact, UNEP Principles for Responsible Banking, and ILO standards. It ensures respect for dignity, health and safety, fair working conditions, diversity and inclusion, training and skills development, and privacy in its work organization choices.
text:
The effectiveness of involvement
Internal climate surveys and feedback collection are carried out by means of focus groups and employee satisfaction 
questionnaires after events, as well as interactive functions on the company intranet (comments, likes, shares).  
Another interaction method was also introduced (“Did you find this article useful?”) to gather colleagues’ views on the 
usefulness and layout clarity of the aspects discussed. 
All employees, based on the methods described, can express their opinion on their working life in the Group, the applica-
tions released and the Bank’s initiatives. 
In parallel, the structured and systematic practice of one-to-one meetings and interviews with employees by Human  
Resource Managers, also at the direct request of the individual employee, has continued. In addition, for new employees, 
targeted listening procedures are in place within the first few months of employment by means of special questionnaires 
to collect their degree of satisfaction and perception on joining the company, as well as feedback interviews during the 
probationary period in which any needs or points of attention are acknowledged. 2024 ANNUAL REPORT - Sustainability Reporting 199

title: Processes to remediate impacts and channels for workers to raise concerns
heading: Processes to remediate impacts and channels for workers to raise concerns
start_phrase: The Group promotes, by means of territorial meetings, moments for exchanging views and the adoption of dialogue structures, the expression of any concerns and needs of its workers.
summary:
- Worker voice and remediation: The Group organizes territorial meetings and dialogue structures to surface concerns and needs, and outlines processes to remediate impacts through reported issues.
- Whistleblowing system: Confidential reporting via a dedicated IT platform or telephone is available to employees and qualified external personnel for suspected violations of laws, regulations, or procedures; reports are received and investigated by the Fraud Audit department.
- Governance link: Further details on complaint handling and protections for whistleblowers are referenced in the Governance section (Policies, objectives and actions related to whistleblowing).
- Training and awareness: A new multimedia whistleblowing course was rolled out in 2024 to all Group personnel, with additional targeted training for owners and new employees.
- Human rights commitment: The Group commits to the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights, UN Global Compact, UNEP Principles for Responsible Banking, the International Bill of Human Rights, and the ILO Declaration, including explicit principles against child and forced labor.
- People-centric policies: Emphasis on enhancing internal skills, professional development, and spreading ESG culture through organizational models that promote growth, shared objectives, and knowledge.
- Workplace protections: Assurance of respect for dignity, health and safety, fair working conditions, diversity and inclusion, training and skills development, and privacy in all work organization choices.
text:
Processes to remediate impacts and channels for workers to raise concerns
The Group promotes, by means of territorial meetings, moments for exchanging views and the adoption of dialogue 
structures, the expression of any concerns and needs of its workers.
The Group provides employees with appropriate tools for reporting possible violations of the rules of conduct (the “Whi-
stleblowing” system). In particular, through the Whistleblowing system, as governed by the Group’s Code of Ethics, each  
employee is required to actively cooperate in the achievement of high ethical standards, both directly - by acting re-
sponsibly - and indirectly - by reporting any violations of laws, regulations and procedures that could have a negative 
impact on the Group. Through the dedicated IT platform or orally via a special telephone service, staff and qualified  
external personnel may report - confidentially - irregular or incorrect circumstances and conduct which they suspect  
or have become aware of in the course of their duties. These reports are received by the Fraud Audit department,  
which is also in charge of internal investigations. For more details on the complaint handling process as well 
as on the policies for the protection of employees using the complaint systems, please refer to Section 4 -  
Information on Governance (par. “Policies, objectives and actions related to whistleblowing”). A new multimedia course  
was implemented in 2024 in which all Group resources were enrolled, in addition to specific training measures for owners 
and new employees.

start_phrase: The Group considers the enhancement of internal skills as a priority, fostering the professional development of its employees.
summary:
- Describes the Group’s mechanisms for workers to raise concerns and remediate impacts, including territorial meetings to encourage dialogue and the formal Whistleblowing system governed by the Code of Ethics.
- Explains that reports can be made confidentially via a dedicated IT platform or telephone, are received by the Fraud Audit department, and may trigger internal investigations; references governance section for complaint handling and protection policies.
- Notes extensive training on ethical conduct and reporting: a new multimedia course in 2024 for all Group personnel, plus specific training for owners and new hires.
- Outlines the Group’s commitment to protecting workers’ human rights and fostering professional development, ESG culture, and organizational models that promote growth, objective sharing, and knowledge.
- Affirms adherence to international standards: UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights, UN Global Compact, UNEP Principles for Responsible Banking, International Bill of Human Rights, and ILO Declaration; rejects child and forced labor.
- Commits to respect for dignity, health and safety, fair working conditions, diversity and inclusion, training and skills development, and privacy.

text:
The Group considers the enhancement of internal skills as a priority, fostering the professional development of its  
employees. To this end, it adopts organisational models aimed at growth, sharing objectives, knowledge and promoting the 
dissemination of an ESG culture at all levels of the organisation, including through compliance with the main international  
agreements and treaties on the subject. In this context, the Group is committed to complying with the United Nations’ 
Universal Declaration of Human Rights, promoting the protection of human rights, including the principles on child labour 
and forced labour, and encouraging a conduct inspired by integrity and respect in line with the UN Global Compact and  
the UNEP Principles for Responsible Banking. These principles refer to the International Bill of Human Rights, as well as 
the International Labour Organisation (ILO) Declaration.
The Group therefore guarantees that people’s lives and dignity are respected, and that work organisation choices  
safeguard the value of individuals, as well as health and safety in the workplace, the protection of working conditions, 
diversity and inclusion, training and skills development, and privacy. BANCA MONTE DEI PASCHI DI SIENA200

title: Social protection - Introduction
heading: Social protection
start_phrase: Employees with a subordinate employment relationship (Italy contract) with one of the companies of the Group are covered against the various cases of loss of employment income by the protections provided by Italian law.
summary: Overview of social protection for Group employees with Italian contracts, detailing legal and collective bargaining coverage by entity. For the Parent Company and Widiba Bank, protections derive from Italian law, the Credit Sector National Collective Bargaining Agreement (CCNL), and the MPS Supplementary Agreement, covering: illness (salary/job preservation up to 36 months by seniority, NASPI indemnity for 24 months after dismissal, child/spouse recruitment on premature death); unemployment (NASPI 24 months); work injury/disability (salary/job preservation up to 36 months, indemnified disability leave, benefits for approaching retirement, NASPI 24 months, insurance for permanent disability/death, child/spouse recruitment on premature death); parental leave (job protection, indemnity, and CCNL salary top-ups); and retirement (extraordinary income support allowance within 5 years of AGO pension entitlement via the credit sector fund, allowance per AGO rules, and supplementary pension via MPS Pension Funds/MPS Fund). For MPS Tenimenti and MPS Magazzini Generali Fiduciari, coverage under their adopted National Collective Bargaining Agreements and Italian law includes similar protections, generally with indemnities of 12/24 months, parental leave with job protection and indemnity (no salary top-ups noted), and retirement allowances per AGO pension rules (no supplementary pension specified).
text:
Social protection
Employees with a subordinate employment relationship (Italy contract) with one of the companies of the Group are  
covered against the various cases of loss of employment income by the protections provided by Italian law. For the Parent 
Company and for Widiba Bank, the provisions of the National Collective Bargaining Agreement (CCNL) for the Credit Sector 
in Italy and of the MPS Supplementary Agreement also apply. For MPS Tenimenti and MPS Magazzini Generali Fiduciari, 
the regulations of the National Collective Bargaining Agreements adopted in those companies apply. More specifically, 
the following covers are provided for the Parent Company and Widiba:
• loss of income due to illness: salary and job preservation for increasing periods based on seniority, up to 36 months 
(Credit Sector CCNL), NASPI indemnity for 24 months following any dismissal (Italian Law), child/spouse recruitment  
in the case of premature death (MPS Supplementary Agreement); 
• loss of income due to unemployment: NASPI indemnity for the 24 months following any dismissal (Italian Law); 
• loss of income due to work injury and resulting disability: preservation of salary and job for increasing periods based on 
seniority, up to 36 months (Credit Sector CCNL), indemnified leave for disability (Italian law), benefits for approaching 
retirement (Italian law), NASPI (New Social Insurance Provision for Employment) indemnity for 24 months following di-
smissal (Italian law), insurance cover for permanent disability/death from accident (Italian law and MPS Supplementary 
Agreement), child/spouse recruitment in case of premature death (MPS Supplementary Agreement); 
• loss of income due to parental leave: job preservation and indemnity for compulsory and optional leave (Italian Law),  
in addition to salary top-ups (Credit Sector CCNL);  
• loss of income due to retirement: extraordinary income support allowance within 5 years of AGO (credit sector  
fund for post-employment benefits) pension entitlement, allowance according to AGO pension rules (Italian law),  
receipt of supplementary pension benefit (MPS Pension Funds / MPS Fund).
The following are the cases provided for by MPS Tenimenti and MPS Magazzini Generali Fiduciari:
• loss of income due to illness: preservation of salary and job for increasing periods according to seniority, indemnity  
for 12/24 months following possible dismissal (Italian law); 
• loss of income due to unemployment: NASPI indemnity for the 12/24 months following any dismissal (Italian Law); 
• loss of income due to work injury and resulting disability: preservation of salary and job for increasing periods based 
on seniority, indemnified leave for disability (Italian law), benefits for approaching retirement (Italian law), indemnity  
for 12/24 months following dismissal (Italian law), insurance cover for permanent disability/death from accident  
(Italian law); 
• loss of income due to parental leave: job preservation and indemnity for compulsory and optional leave (Italian Law); 
• loss of income due to retirement: allowance according to AGO pension rules (Italian law).

title: MPS Pension Funds
heading: MPS Pension Funds
start_phrase: As part of the welfare system provided for by the Group, in relation to the loss of income due to retirement, the MPS Pen- sion Fund and the MPS Welfare Fund have been introduced from 2020 as forms of supplementary pension system, with the possibility of membership also extended to the tax-dependent family members of Group employees.
summary:
- Social protection framework: Employees in Italy across the Group are covered for income loss through Italian law, sector collective agreements (Credit Sector CCNL), and MPS supplementary agreements. Coverage areas include illness, unemployment (NASPI), work injury/disability, parental leave, and retirement, with specifics varying by company.
- Parent Company and Widiba: Enhanced protections such as salary and job preservation up to 36 months (seniority-based), NASPI for 24 months post-dismissal, indemnified disability leave, accident insurance for permanent disability/death, child/spouse hiring in case of premature death, parental leave indemnities with CCNL salary top-ups, and pre-retirement/retirement benefits including extraordinary income support and supplementary pension payments.
- MPS Tenimenti and MPS Magazzini Generali Fiduciari: Similar protections aligned to their applicable national agreements, generally including salary/job preservation based on seniority, indemnities for 12/24 months post-dismissal, disability leave, accident insurance, parental leave protections, and retirement allowances per AGO rules.
- MPS Pension and Welfare Funds: Group supplementary pension schemes (open to employees and tax-dependent family members) managed with ESG criteria; signatories to UN PRI; published policies on stewardship and sustainability risk integration; defined ESG monitoring and reporting. In 2024, aligned with Laws 220/2021 and 122/2022 introducing policies against financing producers of anti-personnel mines/cluster munitions; MPS Pension Fund advanced strategic allocation into private markets via Article 8 and Article 9 SFDR strategies.
- Inclusion of persons with disabilities: 6% of employees are persons with disabilities (52% men, 48% women), hired under Italy’s Law 68/1999 with roles compatible with their conditions. Annual compliance checks determine required hires, coordinated with Employment Centres. The Group also employs other protected categories under Article 18 (e.g., orphans of workers deceased due to work, refugees).
- Training and performance reviews: Near-universal performance review coverage in 2023 across included companies (Parent Company, Widiba, MPS Fiduciaria, MPS Tenimenti, MGFM). By gender: 99.67% of women (8,840) and 99.39% of men (7,663) reviewed; overall 99.54% (16,503 of 16,579). By category: Executive managers 98.73% reviewed (155), Middle Managers 99.87% (6,013), Professional Areas/other 99.37% (10,335).
text:
MPS Pension Funds 
As part of the welfare system provided for by the Group, in relation to the loss of income due to retirement, the MPS Pen-
sion Fund and the MPS Welfare Fund have been introduced from 2020 as forms of supplementary pension system, with 
the possibility of membership also extended to the tax-dependent family members of Group employees. The allocation is 
based on ESG criteria and both funds have been signatories to the UNPRI Protocol (Principles for Responsible Investment ).
Furthermore, in accordance with current regulations, both pension funds have approved and published documents on their 
websites containing information relating to disclosure of the commitment policy and policies incorporation of sustainabili -
ty risks into the investment decision-making processes. The funds also define the monitoring methods and ESG reporting 
plan, for each segment envisaging quantitative analysis of the sustainability factors implemented by specific indicators for 
each aspect: environmental, social and governance.
In 2024, the funds completed the alignment with Law no. 220 of 9 December 2021 as amended following Law no. 122/2022, 
introducing the policy on measures to offset the financing of companies producing anti-personnel mines, cluster muni -
tions and sub-munitions, in a capacity as qualified intermediaries. Furthermore, with reference to the MPS Pension Fund, in 
2024 the strategic asset allocation adjustment activity continued, through planned investing in the private markets with in-
vestment instruments with strategies that explicitly integrate environmental and/or social considerations into investment 
management (Article 8 of the SFDR on sustainability‐related disclosures in the financial services sector, that is part of the 
EU Action Plan for Sustainable Finance) and with products that target sustainable investments (Article 9 of the SFDR - on 
sustainability‐related disclosures in the financial services sector, that is part of the EU Action Plan for Sustainable Finance).BANCA MONTE DEI PASCHI DI SIENA204

text:
Persons with disabilities
The share of own employees with disabilities is 6% (of which 52% men and 48% women).
In particular, these are workers hired in compliance with Law 68/1999 on the compulsory employment of disabled persons 
in Italy, for whom the assignment of tasks compatible with the worker’s disability is envisaged.
The criteria that identify persons considered “disabled” under Law 68/1999 are set out in Article 1 of the Law. Each year,  
in compliance with the regulations in force, the Group checks, on the basis of the overall workforce, the number of disabled 
workers to be included and proceeds, normally in agreement with Employment Centres (Provincial Offices of the Ministry  
of Labour responsible for compulsory employment) to recruit disabled workers. There are also additional workers  
belonging to the “other Protected Categories” referred to in Law 68/1999, Article 18; these are workers for whom, although  
not disabled, a percentage of compulsory recruitment in companies is reserved (e.g. orphans of persons who died  
as a result of work, refugees).

start_phrase: The Group is committed to welfare policies, which aim to create value for people and improve the corporate climate: every aspect of welfare in the Group is aimed at supporting colleagues and their families in financial, social and work/life balance terms, contributing to the increase in satisfaction, wellbeing, loyalty and productivity.
summary:
- Focus on employee welfare and work-life balance: comprehensive policies support employees and their families financially, socially, and in balancing work and life, aiming to boost satisfaction, wellbeing, loyalty, and productivity.
- Collective relations: welfare is central to Level II bargaining with trade unions; extended to employees using the sector Solidarity Fund; benefits apply to all employees regardless of contract type or hours and have expanded over time to cover evolving needs of employees, retirees, and families (over 50,000 people).

- Gender pay equality: overall gender pay gap (average gross hourly male vs. female) is 11.35% for 2024. By role: executives 14.80%; middle managers 6.82%; white-collar -0.91%. The gap has narrowed in recent years.
- Equal pay governance: objective job weighting and measures aligned with EBA Equal Pay Guidelines to promote gender balance and ensure gender-neutral remuneration.
- Pay methodology: gross hourly pay derived from Gross Annual Total Remuneration (ATR) divided by 1,554 theoretical annual hours, neutralizing part-time effects. ATR includes base pay, allowances, benefits (fringe, pensions, insurance), and variable pay for 2023 paid in 2024.
- Pay ratio: Total Remuneration rate of 8.97 (highest-paid employee vs. median of others).
- Human rights and complaints: no lawsuits or extrajudicial proceedings on gender equality violations; eight workplace harassment reports; no judicial/extrajudicial cases on severe human rights incidents.
text:
Work-life balance metrics
The Group is committed to welfare policies, which aim to create value for people and improve the corporate climate: every 
aspect of welfare in the Group is aimed at supporting colleagues and their families in financial, social and work/life balance  
terms, contributing to the increase in satisfaction, wellbeing, loyalty and productivity.
Welfare plays a central role in Level II bargaining, with talks on renewal continuing in 2024, as is a point of reference for all 
colleagues, thanks to ongoing dialogue with the Trade Unions. This model was also extended to personnel making recourse  
to the sector Solidarity Fund and for the entire period of such recourse.
Though within a framework of overall financial compatibility and sustainability, internal welfare has been supplemented  
over time with assets and services that meet the changing needs of employees, retired personnel and their families  
(currently over 50,000 individuals). The benefits are payable to all employees, for all contract types, regardless of working 
hours (part-time or full-time).
All company employees are entitled to family leave. When returning from parental leave, job preservation is fully guaranteed.  
Furthermore, note that parental leave may be taken for children up to the age of 12, in accordance with laws in force.
During 2024, a total of 1,452 employees (or 28% of eligible staff) took parental leave, of whom 325 were men (or 14% of 
eligible men) and 1,127 women (or 37% of eligible women). The return to work rate after maternity/paternity leave was 
around 94%, and those still in service 12 months after the parental leave was around 98%44 (99% for women, 98% for men).

heading: Remuneration metrics (pay gap and total remuneration)
start_phrase: The Group pays special attention to the issue of gender pay equality at all levels.
summary:
- Focus: Sustainability reporting on work-life balance, remuneration equity, and human rights incident metrics.
- Welfare and work-life balance: Comprehensive welfare model to support employees, retirees, and families (50,000+ people), applicable to all employees regardless of contract type or hours; central in Level II bargaining with Trade Unions; extended to those using the sector Solidarity Fund.
- Parental leave: Entitlement for all employees with guaranteed job preservation; usable until a child’s 12th birthday. In 2024, 1,452 employees took leave (28% of eligible staff): 325 men (14% of eligible men) and 1,127 women (37% of eligible women). Return-to-work rate ~94%; 12-month employment retention ~98% overall (99% women, 98% men); slight shortfall due to voluntary resignations.
- Remuneration and pay equity: 2024 gender pay gap (average gross hourly) 11.35% overall; by role—executives 14.80%, middle managers 6.82%, white-collar -0.91%. The Group applies role weighting and measures aligned with EBA Equal Pay guidelines to promote gender neutrality and narrow gaps.
- Methodology: Hourly pay derived from Gross Annual Total Remuneration (ATR) including fringe benefits, pension/insurance company contributions, and variable pay, divided by 1,554 theoretical annual hours to neutralize part-time effects.
- Pay ratio: Highest-paid individual’s Gross ATR to the median of other employees is 8.97.
- Human rights and conduct: No lawsuits or extrajudicial proceedings on gender equality rights; eight workplace harassment reports; no serious human rights incidents reported.
text:
The Group pays special attention to the issue of gender pay equality at all levels. The gender pay gap is defined as  
the difference between the average hourly wage levels paid to female and male workers for the same work. For 2024, the 
percentage delta between the average gross hourly wage of male employees and the average gross hourly wage of female 
employees corresponded to 11.35%.
This ratio was also broken down by type of classification: executives, middle managers and white-collar workers  
and amounted to 14.80%, 6.82% and -0.91% respectively.
This objective approach to the weighting of positions helps to ensure that the remuneration policy is gender neutral  
and makes it possible to pursue equal pay, as evidenced by the narrowing of the gender pay gap in the Group recorded  
in recent years. 
In addition, the Group adopts specific measures and mitigating actions aimed at promoting gender balance and equal pay 
for equal work, equal experience and the other objective elements required by the EBA Guidelines  (Equal Pay).
To determine the gross hourly remuneration, the value of the gross annual total remuneration (Gross ATR) was used45, 
neutralising the distorting effect of more women in part-time work, and dividing the resulting value by the theoretical value 
of the hours worked in the year, equal to 1,554. 
For 2024, the Total Remuneration rate calculated as the ratio of gross annual total Remuneration of the person with the  
highest salary to the median of the Gross ATR of the remaining employees (excluding the aforementioned person) was 8.97.

- Emphasis on employee welfare and work-life balance: comprehensive welfare policies support employees and their families financially, socially, and in work/life balance; accessible to all employees regardless of contract type and extended to personnel using the sector Solidarity Fund. Ongoing Level II bargaining and continuous dialogue with Trade Unions. Benefits cover over 50,000 individuals, including retired personnel and families.

- Family and parental leave: universal entitlement with job preservation on return; parental leave available for children up to age 12. In 2024, 1,452 employees (28% eligible) took parental leave: 325 men (14% of eligible men) and 1,127 women (37% of eligible women). Return-to-work rate ~94%; 12‑month retention ~98% overall (99% women, 98% men), with below‑100% due to voluntary resignations.

- Pay equity and remuneration metrics: the overall gender pay gap based on gross hourly wage is 11.35%; by grade—executives 14.80%, middle managers 6.82%, white-collar -0.91%. The Group applies an objective job‑weighting approach and EBA Equal Pay guidelines, with measures to promote gender balance and equal pay. Gross hourly pay is derived from Gross Annual Total Remuneration (ATR) divided by 1,554 theoretical hours, neutralizing part‑time effects; ATR includes base pay, recurring allowances, fringe benefits, company pension and insurance contributions, and variable pay. Highest-to-median Total Remuneration ratio is 8.97.

- Incidents and human rights: no lawsuits or extrajudicial proceedings on gender equality or serious human rights incidents; eight workplace harassment reports recorded.

- Workers in the value chain (ESRS S2): describes policies, actions, monitoring, and channels for concerns for workers in the value chain, based on a double materiality assessment. Identifies:
  - Negative upstream impacts: potential inadequacy of safeguards on secure employment, working hours, adequate wages, social dialogue, freedom of association, work-life balance, and health and safety.
  - Positive upstream impacts: practices safeguarding health and safety and privacy, and preventing child and forced labour.
  - Notes supplier selection using social sustainability criteria and acknowledges potential impacts from interactions across upstream and downstream value chains.

title: Impacts, Risks and Opportunities
heading: Impacts, Risks and Opportunities
start_phrase: The process of mapping impacts, risks and opportunities with reference to the standard in question includes the spe- cificities related to the Group’s operational and commercial activities, including the analysis of internal policies, public documentation and the identification of initiatives taken to protect employees in the value chain (e.g. selection of suppliers according to social sustainability criteria).
summary:
- Focus: ESRS S2 “Workers in the value chain” within Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena’s 2024 Sustainability Reporting.
- Scope and materiality: Double materiality analysis maps impacts, risks, and opportunities across the value chain; only the upstream value chain is material. Downstream is not material in this assessment.
- Material impacts identified:
  - Potential negative impacts upstream on working conditions: job stability, working hours, adequate wages, social dialogue/freedom of association, work-life balance.
  - Positive impacts upstream from existing corporate practices: safeguarding health and safety, protecting privacy, and preventing child and forced labour.
- Policy framework and governance:
  - Group Code of Ethics guides conduct for subsidiaries, partners, consultants, and suppliers; emphasizes transparency, fairness, integrity, cooperation, and conflict-of-interest avoidance.
  - Suppliers must formally accept adherence to the Code and respect worker rights and social criteria through contractual clauses and general purchasing conditions.
  - Commitment to UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights and principles against child and forced labour; alignment with ILO and OECD standards.
  - Compliance structures: internal control system; Organisation, Management and Control Model under Italian Legislative Decree 231/01 for supplier selection and offence prevention.
  - Additional policies: Occupational Health and Safety Policy; Sustainability and ESG Policy; procurement practices that protect worker H&S, the environment, and people.
- Supplier management and engagement:
  - Supplier selection incorporates occupational health and safety considerations; joint initiatives promoted to manage and resolve risk situations.
  - Ongoing stakeholder engagement with suppliers via the Purchasing Department’s Stakeholder Management process; channels for concerns are referenced through this process.
- Monitoring and outcomes:
  - Processes in place to monitor policy effectiveness; no detected cases of non-compliance with UN Guiding Principles, ILO Declaration, or OECD Guidelines regarding upstream workers.
text:
The process of mapping impacts, risks and opportunities with reference to the standard in question includes the spe-
cificities related to the Group’s operational and commercial activities, including the analysis of internal policies, public  
documentation and the identification of initiatives taken to protect employees in the value chain (e.g. selection of suppliers 
according to social sustainability criteria). Interaction with the Group’s upstream and downstream value chain actors could 
indeed lead to impacts on their workforce, related, for instance, to working hours and work-life balance. On the basis of the 
analyses performed, the following were material: 
• Negative impacts with reference to the Upstream Value Chain perimeter related to the potential inadequacy of  
safeguards to ensure adequate working conditions with reference to work stability, working hours, wage adequacy, 
social dialogue and work-life balance;
• Positive impacts  pertaining to the Upstream Value Chain perimeter related to the existence of corporate practices  
and strategies aimed at safeguarding the health and safety and privacy of workers in the value chain and preventing 
incidents of child and forced labour.
